public_rationale: Reuters reported on September 30, 2026 that Anthropic's calendar-2025 cloud-marketplace sales totaled about $2.16 billion, or 47% of its annual revenue [e1]. That is one company's revenue through a distribution channel, not a reconciled total of realized incremental LLM revenue [e1]. It establishes neither a crossing of $2 trillion under a consistent accounting scope nor a permanent end to the relevant revenue-generating activity [e1]. This historical revenue figure cannot settle whether LLMs will ever generate more than $2 trillion in new revenue [e1].
limitations: The evidence provides no complete lifetime total or reconciled aggregate with defined company coverage, baseline, accumulation period and accounting basis [e1].
Cloud distribution relationships require careful treatment to avoid double counting revenue [e1].
The reported sales do not establish what revenue would justify hyperscaler investment [e1].

public_payload.normalized_proposition: LLMs will never bring in the more than $2 trillion in new revenue required to justify hyperscaler AI spending.

statement.excerpt: On a very rational level, nothing that large language models (LLMs) have done, do or will do in the future can or will ever bring in the more than $2 trillion (or more) in brand new revenue that will be required to make any of this worth it.
statement.document_title: The More You Buy, The More You Lose

from_speaker: nothing that large language models (LLMs) have done, do or will do in the future

our_interpretation: This is an unlimited negative forecast about incremental revenue attributable to LLMs.
The plain reading concerns realized new revenue, not valuation, funding, economic surplus, projected sales or annualized run rate.
No annual period is stated. Cumulative realized incremental revenue is the provisional reading, while annual versus cumulative remains a material ambiguity.
The context concerns returns to hyperscaler investment, but the wording does not clearly restrict whose revenue counts.
'Required to make any of this worth it' is an investment judgment, not an independently specified return threshold.
criteria.support_condition: No finite period of low revenue can establish that the threshold will never be crossed. Support would require a decisive permanent end to the relevant revenue-generating activity with a complete lifetime total at or below USD 2 trillion.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Reliable financial evidence establishes more than USD 2 trillion of realized incremental revenue attributable to LLMs under a consistent, explicitly defined scope.

evidence.explanation: This reports one company's realized marketplace revenue and illustrates why aggregation must account for cloud distribution relationships. It neither measures industry-wide incremental revenue nor establishes a permanent ceiling; Reuters is used because the underlying confidential prospectus was not available in the readable record.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: A dated, verified total exceeding $2 trillion in realized incremental LLM revenue, using defined company coverage, a baseline, a measurement period and consistent accounting without double counting, would contradict the forecast. Support would require a permanent end to the relevant activity and a complete lifetime total at or below $2 trillion.
